objective: Exploratory experiment. (1) Whitney step: test 3-connectivity of the pinwheel law's graph with a vertex at infinity at levels 2-5, so that the law's allowed states determine its planar map up to mirror image. (2) Readability: in the level-7 pinwheel map without labels, find the least radius r at which every interior distinction's label (ticket A's) is a function of its rooted radius-r neighbourhood, for r up to 8; controls: shuffled labels and a non-local fake label must find no such radius.
status: Closed, supported (exploratory, PINWHEEL-NATIVE-20261107-001B-E001): the rule can read its labels from the law. The pinwheel law's graph (with a vertex at infinity) is 3-connected at levels 2-5, so by Whitney the law's allowed states determine its planar map up to mirror image; and every interior distinction's oriented label is a function of its unlabelled radius-2 neighbourhood at levels 5, 6, 7 (up to 235,394 darts, 1,168 neighbourhood types, no conflict), while permuted and non-local labellings conflict on nearly every type. On these patches the pinwheel law grows itself by a local rule that reads only the law.
title: Can the rule read its labels from the law?
